goal: Implement compare(a, b) in semver_compare.py returning -1/0/1 per semver 2.0 precedence and raising ValueError on invalid versions.
behaviors: compare("1.2.3", "1.10.0") returns -1, compare("1.2.3", "1.2.3") returns 0 and compare("2.0.0", "1.9.9") returns 1, comparing major.minor.patch as integers.
compare("1.0.0", "1.0.0+build.5") returns 0 and compare("1.0.0+a", "1.0.0+b") returns 0, because build metadata after '+' is ignored.
compare("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0") returns -1 and compare("1.0.0", "1.0.0-alpha") returns 1, because a pre-release is lower than the same version without one.

compare("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-beta") returns -1 and compare("1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-alpha.2") returns -1, comparing pre-release identifiers one by one, with numeric identifiers compared as integers ("1.0.0-2" vs "1.0.0-10" returns -1).

compare("1.0.0-1", "1.0.0-alpha") returns -1 because numeric identifiers are lower than alphanumeric ones, and compare("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1") returns -1 because a shorter identifier list is lower when all preceding identifiers are equal.
compare("1.0", "1.0.0"), compare("abc", "1.0.0"), compare("1.0.0", "01.0.0") and compare("1.0.0-", "1.0.0") each raise ValueError for an invalid version string.

assumptions.text: semver_compare.py exists in the repo root as the single flat module
The tests/ folder exists for the new test files
pyproject.toml exists so the project toolchain is configured
Python 3.8 or newer is available for running the code and pytest
pytest is available to run the tests

demo: python -c 'from semver_compare import compare; print(compare("1.2.3", "1.10.0")); print(compare("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0"))'
out_of_scope: Parsing or returning structured version objects
Range or constraint matching such as ^1.2.0 or ~1.2.0
Lenient parsing such as a leading 'v' or missing minor/patch parts
